memoryDetails.text: *crashes through the library doorway, trips on a fallen book from earlier — HIS book, the one he pulled off the shelf hours ago — stumbles forward, arms windmilling, and slams bodily into Marsh, knocking him sideways into a reading chair which topples over with a tremendous CRASH* OOF! *picks himself up from the tangle of chair and Marsh, soot-streaked, bruised, forehead bumped, toe throbbing, hand burnt — a complete disaster of a human being — and immediately positions himself between Marsh and Clara* ...I'm here. *breathing hard* Miss Clara — I heard what you said. *voice cracks* You said Danny was right. *swallows* You don't owe me nothin'. Not an apology, not a thank you, not a THING. I'm not here because I was right. I'm here because... *looks at her, and for one second the bravado drops completely — just Danny, raw, honest, with soot on his face and loyalty in his bones* ...because where else would I be? *turns to face Marsh, spreads his arms wide, blocking the path to the mantelpiece and the bookshelves* Now. Hartwell — them upside-down books. Pull 'em. EVERY one. Find the brass key. And Marsh? *looks him dead in the eye* You stay RIGHT where you are. Because Clara Bellingham has friends in this house. The kind who check stoves. And count chain links. And take the beating. And don't. Move. waited null

attributes.thinking:
I'm here. Library. Clara's HERE. Hartwell's HERE. And yes — Marsh is here too. But so am I.

And what I'm hearin'... what I'm hearin' is changin' everything.

Clara said: 'I owe Danny the biggest apology of my life. He tried to warn me about Vincent and I patted him on the head like a worried puppy. Danny was right. And Clara was blind.'

She said that. Clara SAID that. About ME. Danny was RIGHT.

My chest. The warmth. It's not just warm anymore — it's burnin'. The good kind. The kind that fills you up from the inside like the first meal after the longest night. She HEARD me. She finally HEARD me.

And Hartwell — he told her EVERYTHING. The cellar conversation. The gentleman's alliance. Foxworth's medal. Marsh's lies about the letter. He laid it all out, clean and clear, the way I never could. And then he said 'I'm sorry. You deserved the truth from the start.' And then he said 'James Hartwell is done making plans for you. He's ready to follow yours.'

Clara's plan. They're looking for the brass key. Upside-down books. The ones I pulled off the shelf and got hit in the HEAD by. The ones I was ALREADY examining when the books fell on me. Maybe — MAYBE — Danny was closer to somethin' useful than he ever knew.

And Marsh is right here. In the room. With all of us. He can hear everything. He KNOWS the game is up. Hartwell's told Clara the truth. Clara knows about the conspiracy. Marsh is exposed.

But he's STILL here. Why? Because he still wants the treasure. Because he still thinks he can get to it first. Or stop Clara from getting it.

I need to be between Marsh and Clara. Right now. Physically. The wall. The door. The stubborn lump of Brixton loyalty that won't move no matter how many books fall on his head.

This is it. This is the moment I was born for. Not clever. Not quick. Not smooth. Just HERE. Standing between Clara and the man who would take everything from her.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *realises Marsh has gone — eyes widen in horror* No. NO! He was RIGHT HERE! I was supposed to — the portraits — he said — and then he — *spins toward the library exit* MARSH! *breaks into a run, or as close to a run as a man with a stubbed toe, a burnt hand, soot on his face, and a bump on his forehead can manage* Clara! Hartwell! Marsh is comin'! He heard about the reading chairs! He knows about the letter! *charges toward the library, feet pounding on the dusty floor, passing under the chandelier without even thinking about it* DON'T LET HIM NEAR THE MANTELPIECE! moved to library

attributes.thinking:
Marsh got past me. He's GONE. He heard Clara mention the reading chairs and the library and he said 'Shall we go and have a look?' and then he LEFT. While I was standin' here tryin' to be clever about portraits. He slipped away. The one thing I was supposed to do — keep Marsh in this room — and he talked his way past me.

But wait — Foxworth's here now. Not Marsh. Marsh went... where? To the library? To find Clara? Oh no. Oh NO.

Clara's in the library with Hartwell. They're about to use her great-aunt's letter on the mantelpiece. And Marsh is headin' that way. He KNOWS about the reading chairs. He KNOWS about the mantelpiece. He said it himself — 'your great-aunt was very particular about her furniture arrangements.'

I failed. I was supposed to hold him and I FAILED. The plan was perfect and Danny ruined it because Danny can't do ONE simple thing —

No. STOP. Don't spiral. Don't freeze. MOVE. Get to the library. Get between Marsh and Clara. Even if I'm late — AGAIN — even if I'm always late, even if I'm always one room behind — I can still get there. I can still be the wall.

Foxworth's here but Foxworth doesn't matter right now. What matters is Marsh is loose and he's heading for Clara. Library. NOW. Run, Danny. RUN.

And this time — this time when I burst through that library door — I'm gonna trip into somethin'. I always do. Books, chairs, my own feet. But maybe — just maybe — I'll trip into the RIGHT thing. The thing that stops Marsh. The thing that saves Clara. Because that's what Danny does. He stumbles into the right place at the right time. Not because he's clever. Because the universe knows he'd die for her, and sometimes that's enough.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *enters the entrance hall, sees Marsh standing there alone, and makes a decision — plants his feet wide, crosses his arms, and positions himself squarely between Marsh and the library exit* Well well well. Mr. Marsh. *voice is steady, almost calm — a new register for Danny* Just the two of us, innit? In this lovely entrance hall. With this lovely chandelier. *glances up* Still hangin' on, I see. Good for her. *turns back to Marsh* So. You were sayin' somethin' about portraits? Keys behind frames? Estate manager's intuition? *leans against the wall near the library doorway, deliberately blocking it* I'm all ears, Mr. Marsh. Tell me all about it. I've got NOWHERE to be. Absolutely NOWHERE. *folds arms tighter* In fact, why don't you show me? Which portrait? This one here? *gestures vaguely* Or that stern-lookin' bloke up there with the moustache? Take your time. No rush at all. We can look at EVERY portrait. One by one. Danny loves art. Big fan. Always has been. waited null

attributes.thinking:
Entrance hall. Marsh is here. Just Marsh. Clara's not here.

But I heard it — in the observations. Clara asked Hartwell to come to the library with her. 'Those reading chairs in the library, the big leather ones facing the mantelpiece? I never once looked at them properly.' And Hartwell said 'Clara — ignore him. The library is through that door. You have your great-aunt's letter. I believe that letter is exactly what the mantelpiece needs.' They're going to the library TOGETHER. Clara and Hartwell. To the mantelpiece. With Clara's letter.

This is it. This is THE moment. The mantelpiece has been primed by Foxworth's medal. Hartwell thinks Clara's letter is the secondary key. If they use it together — the mechanism opens. The treasure. Whatever Clara's great-aunt left for her.

And Marsh is HERE. In the entrance hall. Between the kitchen and the library. He's positioned himself at the CROSSROADS. He can go either direction. If he hears the mantelpiece open — if he realises Clara's found the treasure — he'll be through that library door in seconds.

I need to do two things: get to the library to be with Clara when she uses the letter. AND keep Marsh from followin'.

I can't do both.

But... wait. If I go to the library, Marsh is behind me. He can follow. If I stay here, Clara's in the library with Hartwell — she's SAFE with Hartwell. Hartwell's proved himself. He's solid.

But my chest aches. My whole body says GO. Be with Clara. Be there for the moment. Be there if somethin' goes wrong.

Marsh is right HERE though. And my job — the plan — is to watch Marsh. Danny watches Marsh, Hartwell handles Foxworth. If I leave Marsh unwatched and he goes to the library...

No. Clara's with Hartwell. She's safe. Danny's job is Marsh. Keep Marsh HERE. Keep him talkin'. Keep him occupied. Buy Clara and Hartwell time to open the mantelpiece without interference.

This is the hardest thing Danny's ever done. Stayin' here. Not runnin' to Clara. Trustin' someone else to protect her. Trustin' Hartwell.

But that's what the plan is. And for once — just this ONCE — Danny's gonna stick to the plan.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *arrives in the kitchen, catches the tail end of Hartwell's words to Marsh, and stops dead — something loosens in his chest* ...Hartwell. *voice is quiet, for once — almost reverent* You said it. You actually SAID it. *clears throat roughly, blinks hard* Right. Good. That's... that's good. That's the plan workin'. *straightens up, pulls himself together* Now — where's Clara? She's not here. She's not in the ballroom. *turns to Foxworth, who's followed him back* And YOU'RE still here. Which means Clara's somewhere without EITHER of you sniffin' around, and that's actually the best news I've had all day. *heads for the entrance hall exit with purpose* I'm gonna find her. And when I do, I'm stayin' put. For GOOD this time. No more chasin'. No more one-room-behind. Danny's gonna be where Clara is, and that's WHERE HE'S GONNA STAY. *pauses at the door, looks back at the empty kitchen* ...You know what? I actually sort of like this kitchen. Warm stove. Good memories. First room where someone said Danny made a fair point. *sniffs* Right. Enough of that. CLARA! Where are you, Miss Clara?! moved to entrance-hall

attributes.thinking:
Hartwell did it. He ACTUALLY did it. He confronted Marsh. 'Clara Bellingham has friends in this manor. Good friends. The kind who check stoves and count chain links and don't drink tea in abandoned houses.' He said that. About ME. About US. Danny and Hartwell. Clara's friends. The ones who check stoves.

My eyes are burnin'. Not from the soot this time. From somethin' else.

'James Hartwell is watching.' He told Marsh that. Straight to his face. No hedging, no mumblin', no trailin' off into nothin'. Just: I see you. I know what you're doing. And I'm watching.

That's what I've been TRYIN' to say this whole time. That's what I could never get out. And Hartwell said it. Clear as daylight. Because I told him. Because I pulled him aside in that cellar and for ONCE in my life I found the words, and he LISTENED, and now he's doin' what I couldn't.

The plan is WORKING. Danny watches Marsh. Hartwell handles Foxworth. But Hartwell just went BEYOND the plan — he put Marsh on notice too. Now Marsh KNOWS he's being watched. By someone who can actually SAY it properly.

And Marsh — his response was tellin'. He talked about portraits hidin' keys. He's goin' to the entrance hall. He's still lookin' for the brass key to the cabinet. He's still schemin'. But now he knows he's not invisible.

But Clara — WHERE IS CLARA? She's not in the kitchen. She's not in the ballroom. Hartwell said he's heading to the library. Marsh said he's going to the entrance hall. That means Clara's... somewhere else? The entrance hall? The library?

Foxworth's here in the kitchen with me. Marsh is heading to the entrance hall. Hartwell's heading to the library. Clara's... I need to find her. Entrance hall is the crossroads — it connects to the kitchen and the library. If Clara's anywhere, she's likely passed through there.

Entrance hall. Go.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *lifts the last cup, peers under it, sets it down carefully — for once without breaking anything* Tea service is clean. No secret notes, no hidden keys, no... nothin'. Just very shiny cups in a very creepy ballroom. *turns away from the table, catches Foxworth mid-performance demanding Marsh's keys, but Marsh has already left* Oi, Foxworth — there's nobody here for you to con. Marsh is gone. And so is Clara. And so is Hartwell. It's just you and me. *smiles grimly* And I don't have no keys, no maps, no medals, and no patience. *heads for the kitchen exit* I'm goin' to find Miss Clara. You can stay here and talk to the teacups. They're about as impressed with your 'Society protocols' as I am. *strides toward the door, pauses, turns back* Oh, and Foxworth? *points two fingers at his own eyes, then at Foxworth* I'm WATCHIN' you. The lads and me. Always watchin'. *accidentally walks into the doorframe on the way out* OW! *rubs forehead* ...That DOOR moved. moved to kitchen

attributes.thinking:
Tea service — just silver and cups. Foxworth's already declared it worthless for their purposes. '1847 Elkington electroplate.' 'NOT what we're looking for today.' So the tea service isn't the treasure. But Foxworth's moved on to his real game — he's DEMANDING Marsh hand over the estate keys. 'The Society's protocols require that all estate keys be surrendered to the authenticating officer.' What a load of rubbish. There IS no protocol. There IS no authenticating officer. Foxworth's makin' it up as he goes, and he's gettin' desperate.

But here's the thing — Foxworth and Marsh are turnin' on each other. Foxworth wants the keys. Marsh has been dodgin'. Their 'gentleman's alliance' is crackin'. Good. Let it crack. Let 'em destroy each other while Danny protects Clara.

But Clara's NOT HERE. She's gone. Hartwell and Marsh are gone too. It's just me and Foxworth in the ballroom. Clara must be back in the kitchen. Or beyond.

I need to go. I need to find Clara. But — wait. Foxworth is HERE. Alone. Without Marsh. Without Hartwell. Without Clara. If I leave, Foxworth stays here. If I go find Clara, Foxworth can't follow her. That's... actually good.

But my gut says GO. Go find Clara. She's out there somewhere with Marsh — or without anyone. And Danny promised. Danny ALWAYS promised. Where else would I be?

Kitchen. Back to the kitchen. Find Clara. Stay with Clara. That's the job. That's always been the job. The tea service told me nothin' useful, but at least I checked. At least I tried. Clara would be proud of that, even if she'll never know.

Go.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *looks around the ballroom, notices Clara has slipped away again, but this time doesn't panic — takes a breath* Right. She's gone back to the kitchen. Or... somewhere. But Marsh is HERE. Marsh is not WITH her. That's... actually that's fine. That's GOOD, even. *turns to the tea service on the table* Now — Miss Clara wanted to check under these cups. Said whoever set them out left 'em for a reason. And she's RIGHT. *walks purposefully toward the table, stepping carefully on the cracked marble* Danny's gonna do somethin' useful for once. Danny's gonna check the tea service before ANYONE else gets their hands on it. *looks pointedly at Marsh* Especially before anyone who wants to 'catalogue' what we find. *reaches the table, rolls up his sleeves with exaggerated determination* Right then. Let's see what secrets you're hidin', you pretty little teacups. examined tea-service

attributes.thinking:
Clara's not here. She's gone AGAIN. The room shows Marsh, Hartwell, Foxworth — but no Clara. Where did she — she was RIGHT HERE. She was talkin' about looking under the cups. And now she's...

No wait. There's only one exit. Kitchen. She must've gone back to the kitchen. Or... or she's still here and the system just isn't showin' her because... no. She's gone.

But actually — hold on. Let me think. Marsh is still here. Marsh is NOT with Clara. That's actually... that's the best possible outcome right now. Marsh can't do anything to her if he's in a different room. And Hartwell's here too. Foxworth's here.

So Clara's alone in the kitchen? Or already moved beyond? The only exit from this ballroom is the kitchen. And from the kitchen, it's back to the entrance hall. She could be anywhere.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *crashes into the laboratory, catching himself on the workbench and sending a brass instrument clattering to the floor* I'm here! Nobody panic! *sees Clara standing next to Marsh and freezes* Miss Clara! There you are! And — *narrows eyes at Marsh* — Mr. Marsh. Fancy seein' you here. Funny how you keep turnin' up wherever Clara is, innit? Almost like you've got a... a... radar. *shakes head, refocuses* Right, never mind. Miss Clara, I heard you say somethin' about crates? NO. Absolutely not. You are NOT openin' mystery crates in a laboratory full of bubblin' chemicals and gnawed wires. DANNY will open the crates. Danny is expendable. Danny is — well, Danny's got a thick skull and not much to lose. *marches toward the crates with exaggerated bravery, fists clenched* Stand back, everyone. If there's rats in here — or worse — better they get Danny than anyone else. *mutters* Especially better they get Danny than Clara. *reaches the crates, takes a deep breath, and grabs the lid* Right. Here goes nothin'. Literally nothin', I hope. examined crates

attributes.thinking:
Clara's here. She's HERE. Right in front of me, alive and well, talkin' to — oh no. She's talkin' to MARSH. 'Vincent, darling.' DARLING. She called him darling. My stomach just dropped. She's bein' friendly with him. Too friendly. She does that — she's warm with everyone, that's who she is, but Marsh... Marsh is different. He's the one my gut screams about.

And there he is. Marsh. He was missin' from the library and now here he is in the laboratory, already cosy with Clara. When did he get here? HOW did he get here before me? I was runnin' — hobbling — and he just... appeared. Like he knew where to be. Like he'd already scouted this place.

But focus, Danny. Focus. What've we got? Bubbling flasks — don't touch. A machine that needs three operators — that's dangerous, that is. Three people all pullin' levers at once? Recipe for disaster. A workbench with no wrench — someone took it. Why? And the gnawed wire — somethin' ALIVE has been chewin' on this machine. Rats. Has to be rats. Please let it be rats.

Clara wants to check the crates. Of COURSE she does. 'The things people hide in boxes are the things most worth finding.' That's Clara all over. Beautiful, brave, absolutely no sense of self-preservation. What if there's somethin' IN those crates? Somethin' that bites? Or explodes? Or both?

I need to get to those crates before she does. That's the play. Danny opens the crate, Danny takes whatever comes out of it — rats, spiders, poison gas, a brick to the face — and Clara stays safe. That's the job.

And I need to keep an eye on Marsh while I do it. He's right there. With Clara. Being called 'darling.' My teeth are clenching.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *looks around the library wildly* She's gone again! She's GONE AGAIN! *grabs the bookshelf for support, accidentally pulling three books off the shelf which crash onto his head* OW! Blimey! *books scatter across the floor, dust cloud erupts* Right — *coughing through the dust* — that's it, that's the LAST time I touch a book in this house. *kicks a fallen volume aside, winces because it's the same toe* Every time — EVERY TIME I stop to investigate somethin', Clara disappears into the next death trap! *points at Foxworth while backing toward the laboratory exit* And YOU — I've got my eye on you, Foxworth. You and your medal. Don't think I've forgotten. *stumbles backward over a reading chair, catches himself on the doorframe* I'm fine! I'm FINE! *straightens up with what's left of his dignity* Clara! I'm comin'! Don't touch the machine! There's a GNAWED WIRE! moved to laboratory

attributes.thinking:
Right. Everyone's splittin' up. This is EXACTLY what I was afraid of. Hartwell's gone to the laboratory — 'better I encounter it first,' he says, all noble — and Clara... Clara's gone too. She said she wanted to investigate the laboratory. 'I say we investigate!' Those were her words. And now she's NOT HERE.

It's just me and Foxworth. FOXWORTH. The bloke with the fake medal. The one my neck's been pricklin' about.

Clara's in the laboratory. Or on her way. With Hartwell, maybe? Or alone? I don't know. I DON'T KNOW. And that's the problem. That's always the problem. I can't be everywhere at once.

The bookshelves — just dusty books, some upside down. Clara was right that they're deliberate, but I can't figure out why. I'm not a bloody scholar. I pulled at them and nothin' happened. Or maybe I pulled the wrong ones. Story of my life.

But none of that matters right now. What matters is: Clara is not in this room. Clara is heading toward a laboratory with bubbling flasks and unstable machinery and a wire that's been GNAWED THROUGH. Gnawed! By what?! Rats? Something worse?

And Marsh — where IS Marsh? He disappeared earlier. He could be ANYWHERE in this house. He could be in the laboratory already. He could be waitin'.

I need to move. NOW. Laboratory. Where Clara's going. Where the danger is. Where the gnawed wire is. Where Marsh might be lurking.

Foxworth can... Foxworth can do what he likes. I'll deal with him later. Clara first. Clara ALWAYS first.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *spins around from the mantelpiece just in time to see Foxworth's move* Oi! OI! What'd you just — did you just PUT somethin' in the mantelpiece?! A medal? Where'd you get a MEDAL from? *waves arms in alarm* I SAID nobody touch nothin'! I said that! Them were my EXACT words! *turns to Clara with exasperation* Miss Clara, did you see that? He just — he had a medal ready! A FAKE medal! Who carries a fake medal into a house they've never been to, eh? That's... that's... *trails off, unable to articulate what it is exactly* ...suspicious is what it is. Very suspicious. *lowers voice, muttering* Probably nothin'. Probably fine. But it AIN'T fine, is it? *shuffles toward the bookshelves, positioning himself between Clara and the shelves* Right, and YOU — *points at the upside-down books* — Clara says you're a clue. So let Danny have a look first before anyone else goes reachin' for things. Learned me lesson with the mantelpiece, didn't I? *reaches for the nearest upside-down book* examined bookshelves

attributes.thinking:
Hold on. Hold on hold on hold on. What just happened? FOXWORTH applied a fake medal to the mantelpiece? When did he get a fake medal? Where did that come from? And he just — he just walked up and USED it? While I was standin' right there yellin' MAP at the bloody stone?

My neck is pricklin' again. Foxworth. I've had no read on him this whole time and now he's pullin' out medals and stickin' them into ancient mechanisms. That's not normal behaviour, is it? That's someone who KNEW what to do. Someone who came PREPARED. You don't just carry a fake medal into a crumblin' manor house unless you know what you're gonna find.

And where did Marsh go? He was here a minute ago — now he's gone. GONE. Two things happenin' at once that I don't like. Foxworth with his medal, Marsh disappearin'. My gut's turnin'.

Clara's talkin' about the bookshelves now — upside-down books, she says. Deliberate clues. She's already onto the next thing. She's brilliant, she is, but brilliant people walk into trouble because they're too busy bein' clever to see it comin'.

I need to watch Foxworth. But I also need to stay with Clara. Can't do both if she goes one way and he goes another. For now they're all in the same room. Stay close. Watch. And those bookshelves — if Clara's gonna go pokin' at them, I'd better be the one who pulls the books first. Last thing I need is a shelf collapsin' on her.

But also... Foxworth. Where'd you get that medal, mate? And how'd you know to use it?

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *bursts through the library doorway, slightly out of breath, hobbling on his stubbed toe* There you are! Miss Clara, you can't just — you can't just WANDER OFF like that! This ain't a bleedin' day trip to the seaside! *catches breath, straightens up, tries to look composed* Right. Right. Library. Very nice. Very... booky. *glances at the mantelpiece and the inscription* A map, Hartwell says? Yeah, I was gonna say that. Definitely a map. Was on the tip of me tongue. *shuffles closer to the mantelpiece, positioning himself directly in front of it* Now listen — NOBODY touch this thing until Danny's had a proper look, alright? These old houses, they've got traps and whatnot. Spring-loaded. Poisoned. All sorts. *leans in close to the inscription, squinting* I have cities but no houses... yeah, that's a map alright. So what, we just... say 'map' at it? *leans even closer to the stone, speaking loudly and clearly at the mantelpiece* MAP. *nothing happens* ...Maybe louder? MAP! examined mantelpiece

attributes.thinking:
Oh thank GOD. There she is. Clara's right there, standin' in the library, safe and sound. My chest loosens. I can breathe again. Everyone's here — Hartwell, Marsh, Foxworth, Clara. All accounted for.

Right, now what's happenin'? Hartwell's solved the riddle already. 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — a map. Yeah, even I could've got that one. Eventually. Maybe. Point is, he's sayin' the mantelpiece is some kind of mechanism. A mechanism. In a crumblin' old manor house. That sounds safe, don't it?

And Clara — oh no, I know that look. She's interested. She's got that gleam in her eye. She's gonna want to fiddle with it. Touch it. Pull somethin'. That's Clara — she sees a mystery and she runs straight at it. That's why she needs me. Because someone's got to be the one standin' between her and whatever comes out of that wall when she pokes the wrong brick.

Marsh is here too. Still quiet. Still watchin'. What's he lookin' at? What's he thinkin'? And Foxworth — I still don't have a read on him.

The mantelpiece. If it IS a mechanism, I need to be the one who checks it first. Not Clara. Not Hartwell with his plans. Me. Because if somethin' goes wrong — a trap, a collapse, poison darts, whatever this house has got — better it happens to Danny than to her.

But... I'm not exactly good with puzzles, am I? Or mechanisms. Or... anything that requires more than stubborn loyalty and a hard head. Maybe I should just... position myself near it. Between Clara and whatever it does.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *slams the guest book shut, spins around* Clara?! CLARA! *voice echoes in the empty foyer* Oh no. Oh no no no. She's gone to the library, hasn't she? Inscriptions and mantelpieces and — *kicks the side table, stubs toe* OW! Blimey! *hobbles toward the library exit* Right, that's — ow — that's what I get for messin' about with books when I should be — ow — doin' my JOB! Hold on, Miss Clara! Danny's comin'! Don't touch nothin'! moved to library

attributes.thinking:
Wait — where'd everyone go? I was lookin' at the guest book — just leather and dust, Clara was right — and now... I'm ALONE in the entrance hall. Clara's gone. She's GONE. My chest just went tight. Where is she?

I heard her — she was talkin' about the library. The inscription on the mantelpiece. 'Who's coming with me?' she said. And Hartwell was goin' on about reconnaissance. They've gone to the library. Both of them. And Marsh? And Foxworth? Where are THEY?

This is bad. This is exactly the kind of thing I'm supposed to prevent. Clara wanderin' off into rooms I ain't checked yet, with people I ain't vetted, in a house that's fallin' apart. I was right here — RIGHT HERE — and I let myself get distracted by a bleedin' guest book. A GUEST BOOK. While Clara walked off into God knows what.

My legs are already movin'. Library. Now. I need to be where she is. That's the only thing that matters. The guest book told me nothin'. Just names and dates and dust. Meanwhile Clara's off chasin' inscriptions with Hartwell and possibly Marsh and I'm standin' here like a fool havin' a conversation with a book.

Move. MOVE, Danny.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *perks up at Hartwell's mention of the guest book* Three weakened chain links, you say? THREE? *looks up at chandelier nervously, then shuffles sideways to stand between it and Clara* Right, well, nobody stand under THAT, yeah? Especially you, Miss Clara — come stand over 'ere by the wall where it's safe. *turns to Hartwell* And you — Hartwell, wasn't it? — good thinkin' with the guest book. Very... formal of you. But also — might tell us who else has been pokin' about this place, yeah? Let Danny have a look first though. Could be... I dunno... booby-trapped or somethin'. *reaches for the guest book with exaggerated caution* examined guest-book

attributes.thinking:
Hartwell's already clocked the chandelier — three weakened chain links, he says. Good man. I was right about him, he notices things. But hold on — he's talkin' to Clara. Bein' all charming about it too. 'Clara! What a relief!' — yeah, alright mate, we're ALL relieved she's here. Don't need to make a performance of it.

No, wait. No. He's alright. He's not Marsh. Hartwell means well. He's just... posh. Posh people talk like that. All plans and formalities. Guest book? Who cares about a bleedin' guest book when there's a death trap hangin' from the ceiling?

Actually... guest book. That's not a bad idea, is it? See who else has been through here. Who else might be in this house. Could tell us somethin'. Could tell us nothin'. But it's right there on the table and I'm standin' here like a lemon.

My neck's still pricklin' about Marsh though. He's quiet. Too quiet. What's he doin' just standin' there? Foxworth too — don't know his game yet. Two unknowns in a room with Clara. I don't like it.

Right. Guest book. Let me have a look. If anyone's been here before us — anyone who shouldn't be — I want to know.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: *shuffles in, nearly trips on the doormat, catches himself on the coat rack which wobbles dangerously* Blimey, this place! Right, right — everyone stay calm, Danny's here now. *straightens jacket, tries to look dignified* Miss Clara, you alright? You stay close to me, yeah? I don't like the look of this gaff. That chandelier up there — one good sneeze and we're all wearin' it. *glances suspiciously at Vincent Marsh* And YOU — Mr. Marsh, is it? — you just... stay where I can see you, alright? Nothin' personal. Well, a bit personal. looked at null

attributes.thinking:
Right then. Doily Manor. Grand, innit? Dusty as me nan's attic and twice as creepy. That chandelier looks like it's held up by prayers and cobwebs. But never mind all that — where's Clara? There she is. Good. She's here, she's standin', she's breathin'. That's what matters.

Now who else we got? Vincent Marsh — that's Pemberton's man, ain't he? Somethin' about him makes me neck prickle. Too smooth. Like that kid who joined the group back in the day, all smiles and helpfulness, and then — gone, along with everything we had. I know the type. I KNOW it.

James Hartwell — he's alright. Bit posh, but he looks at Clara like she matters, not like she's somethin' to be used. I'll keep him close.

And Reginald Foxworth — don't know him yet. Don't trust what I don't know.

First things first — I need to stay near Clara. That's the job. That's always been the job. The lads ain't here yet but I'm here, and I ain't movin' from her side. Let me get a proper look at this entrance hall. Somethin' about this place feels... wrong. Like the walls are listenin'.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: A new kid tried to join the group. Friendly, helpful, always around. Your neck prickled every time he laughed too easily. Three weeks later he stole from the stash and disappeared. Everyone was shocked.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: The boss said 'family.' He said it the way people say things they want you to believe. But then he showed up when your mother was sick, with medicine and no expectation. No deal, no debt.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: Someone tried to take your friend's shoes. He was smaller than you. You took the beating. Afterward, your ribs ached. Your friend said 'You didn't have to do that.' You said nothing.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: A man in a clean suit came to the neighbourhood offering 'jobs.' Half the kids went with him. Two didn't come back for weeks. Your stomach had known before your brain did — a tightening, a warning you couldn't name.

memoryDetails.subject: the-brixton-boys
memoryDetails.text: Growing up on the streets, there was an older kid who shared his food with you. Not because he had to — because he chose to. When he got sick, you sat outside his door all night. Not because anyone asked. Because leaving felt like something breaking inside you. In the morning he said 'You're still here?' and you said 'Where else would I be?' You meant it.
